subject: Follow-up: Private/VPC deployment pricing, env counts & unit-econ targets
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Park <jon.park@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Private/VPC deployment pricing, env counts & unit-econ targets

Jon — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and the handful of items we need to size a Private/VPC proposal that aligns with Healthlytics' budget and compliance needs.

Summary of the call:
- Healthlytics is exploring a Private (VPC) deployment to host PHI-containing inference for the patient triage product.
- Primary asks: predictable unit economics, support SLA (24/7 for production), and KMS integration for keys.

Information we need to finalize a proposal (can reply in-line):
1) Token volumes (monthly): steady-state and peak/spike month estimates (we use tokens = input+output on avg).
2) Target budget range (monthly or annual) you want us to target for the platform + support.
3) Preferred licensing model: committed reserved capacity (GPU-pools) vs hybrid (baseline license + per-1M token overage).
4) Desired support tier: Standard / Premium / Enterprise (Enterprise includes 24/7 and named technical contact).
5) Number of environments to provision initially (prod, staging, dev, sandbox, etc.).
6) Any compliance constraints beyond SOC2 (e.g., HIPAA BAA, on-prem air gap windows).
7) Target unit price (your target $/1M tokens) if you have one — helps us tune committed vs usage pricing.

Attachments: draft licensing options (Redwood-Private-licensing-options.pdf) and a short SOW stub (SOW_v1.pdf). I’ll start a draft quote after you confirm the bullets above.

Next steps we propose:
- If you can send the numbers above, Neha will prepare a baseline quote + recommended env layout.
- Option: 30-day pilot (we can do a dedicated pilot slab) to validate latency and token econ before a long-term commit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min follow to walk through the options.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[e] evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | [m] +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jon Park <jon.park@healthlytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthlytics.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 01:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private/VPC deployment pricing, env counts & unit-econ targets

Evelyn — thanks for the recap, that matches what we discussed. Answers below.

1) Token volumes (rough monthly):
- Steady-state: ~25M tokens / month (mostly inference for triage flows)
- Peak month (marketing/seasonal): expect up to ~120M tokens / month for short windows

2) Budget range: roughly $15k–$30k / month for platform + support depending on commitment and SLA.

3) Licensing preference: we prefer a committed model for baseline predictability (reserved GPU pools) but are open to a hybrid commit + overage if the math is favorable.

4) Support: Enterprise (named TAM + 24/7 escalation).

5) Environments: initial ask is 3 environments (prod, pre-prod/staging, dev). We may add a sandbox later.

6) Compliance: HIPAA (we will need a BAA) and SOC2 Type II. We also need KMS integrations and audit log retention for 1 year.

7) Target unit price: internal stakeholders would like pricing around $900 / 1M tokens as a starting negotiation point, assuming reasonable committed baseline.

Procurement asked to loop in security for the BAA requirements — adding them shortly. Also: what is the minimum term you generally require for a committed slab?

Jon
Director, Product — Healthlytics
jon.park@healthlytics.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Park <jon.park@healthlytics.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private/VPC deployment pricing, env counts & unit-econ targets

Jon — great detail, appreciate it. Based on the numbers you shared, here is a recommended structure we typically propose for customers with similar profiles:

Proposed commercial (high level):
- Baseline: reserved capacity slab sized to handle ~30M tokens/month steady-state (covers average + buffer) delivered via dedicated GPU pool.
- Pilot: optional 30-day pilot slab with reduced commit (we can size to 10M tokens / month) to validate perf & latency. Pilot pricing is discounted and converts to part of initial commit if you proceed.
- Hybrid overage: committed slab covers baseline; overages billed per 1M tokens at an overage rate.

Indicative numbers (illustrative, subject to final infra sizing):
- Baseline license fee (reserved slab) + support (Enterprise): $12k–$18k / month (covers up to ~30M tokens).
- Overage: $950 / 1M tokens over the committed slab.
- Onboarding / integration (one-time): $25k (includes KMS integration guidance and runbook).
- Term: 12- or 24-month options; longer term reduces unit price.

If you target $900 / 1M tokens as your negotiation anchor, we can move the overage closer to that with a modest increase in baseline commit (e.g., a 40–50M tokens baseline commitment over 12–24 months).

I attached a draft quote for internal review (quote-draft-Healthlytics-20270509.pdf). Next steps I propose:
- Evelyn to share pilot scope doc (I will attach a quick pilot scope).
- If procurement is comfortable, we’ll produce a formal quote with a couple of term options (12/24) and include the BAA and SOC2 references.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

From: procurement@healthlytics.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private/VPC deployment pricing, env counts & unit-econ targets

Thanks Neha — procurement needs a unitized breakdown for committed vs overage (we need to model both conservative and aggressive usage scenarios). Please include:
- Per-1M token price at 12m term for three commit tiers (30M, 50M, 100M baseline / month).
- Overage price per 1M tokens and how it's measured (daily rolling, hourly).
- Any volume discounts or stepped pricing.
- Data residency & KMS/HSM integration options (we will need a short design note).

Also confirm minimum term for reserved capacity and cancellation terms. Security will validate the BAA and SOC2 paperwork once we see the SOW.

procurement@healthlytics.com

Thanks — understood. I’ll pull together the tiered per-1M breakdown and a short note on KMS/HSM options (we support customer-managed KMS + HSM key wrapping; will provide a succinct integration checklist). Attached: pilot scope (pilot-scope.docx) and the SOW stub (SOW_v1.pdf) for security/procurement to start reviewing.

Proposed short timeline:
- Today: send tiered pricing + KMS note + draft quote (we will include 12 and 24 month options).
- Thu this week: 30-min follow-up to review the numbers and confirm which commit tier you want to test in pilot.
- After pilot: convert to binding commitment or iterate on baseline sizing.

I’ll also send calendar invites for Thu; if you prefer a different cadence, say so. DocuSign-ready quote will follow once we agree to a baseline slab.

Best —
Evelyn
